title: Why Idempotency Matters in Distributed Systems
explanation: Idempotency means that repeating an operation produces the same final result as performing it once. It is especially important in distributed systems, where network failures can cause clients to retry requests. For example, a payment API should not charge a customer twice when the same request is accidentally submitted multiple times. Developers commonly solve this with unique idempotency keys and server-side request tracking. This makes APIs more reliable and protects important operations against duplicate execution.
takeaway: Design retryable operations carefully. Idempotency helps prevent duplicate actions and makes distributed applications more reliable.
author: MUHAMMAD JUNAEID
